title: Why do U.S. homes have those little doors near the floor?

lines.text: Have you ever explored an older American house and spotted a mysterious tiny door near the floor?
lines.caps: Why do older US homes have *tiny | doors near the *floor?

lines.text: No, they weren't built for secret pets or tiny fairy visitors.
lines.caps: Not built for *secret pets | or fairy *visitors!

lines.text: In the early twentieth century, these small exterior-facing hatches were milk delivery doors.
lines.caps: In the early 1900s, these were *milk | delivery *hatches

lines.text: Every morning, local milkmen placed fresh glass bottles of cold milk into the insulated compartment from outside.
lines.caps: Milkmen placed fresh *bottles | inside from the *outside

lines.text: Families could open the interior latch from the kitchen without ever stepping outside into winter snow.
lines.caps: Homeowners retrieved milk *inside | without facing winter *snow!

lines.text: Other floor-level doors led to coal chutes or laundry chutes dropping straight into the basement furnace room.
These vintage doors are charming relics of everyday American life before modern grocery stores.
